method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

items.assessment: Supporting lower legs to float heels directly fixes the observed failure of a knee pillow. Thigh support, softer linen and massage do not remove sustained heel contact; clear application cue.
Key is appropriate but specialty-mattress-rules-out injury is a giveaway. Use realistic equipment-focused responses and parallel conclusions.
issues: Key is appropriate but specialty-mattress-rules-out injury is a giveaway. Use realistic equipment-focused responses and parallel conclusions.

options: The turning interval can be lengthened if the mattress is functioning
The whole prevention plan needs reassessment
The discomfort should settle once the client adapts to the surface
Adding folded blankets is the best way to improve the mattress effect
why: Equipment function does not establish individual tissue tolerance.
A support surface does not remove the need for individualized positioning.
New discomfort requires assessment rather than assumed adaptation.
Extra layers can interfere with intended pressure redistribution; review the whole plan.

items.assessment: Lowest clinically appropriate elevation plus assisted repositioning addresses sliding/shear without abandoning required elevation. Dragging and extra layers are relevant technique errors.
Bed rest for every activity and stopping all shifts are excessive. Use plausible reminder/cushion approaches that miss the observed forgetting barrier.
issues: Bed rest for every activity and stopping all shifts are excessive. Use plausible reminder/cushion approaches that miss the observed forgetting barrier.

options: Review the weight-shift technique once at the next appointment
Ask the client to shift when discomfort first develops
Replace the cushion before evaluating how reminders work
Agree on reminders within the activity routine
why: The skill is present; the immediate barrier is remembering during activities.
Waiting for symptoms may not provide timely pressure relief, particularly with reduced sensation.
Equipment review may be appropriate, but a new cushion does not address forgetting an effective prescribed skill.
Cues support sustained use of an effective existing skill.

items.assessment: Assessment question mixes a diagnosis and two only-options. Use parallel assessment domains.
issues: Assessment question mixes a diagnosis and two only-options. Use parallel assessment domains.

options: The mattress type and its maintenance history
Time spent supine since the last assisted turn
Distribution and exposure to stool
The number and location of previous pressure injuries
why: Support-surface information is relevant to pressure prevention but less direct for a stool-exposure pattern.
Duration of pressure matters but does not best distinguish the diffuse superficial perineal irritation described.
The pattern may indicate moisture-associated skin damage.
Past injury informs risk but does not characterize the current irritant distribution.

items.assessment: Two only-options cue SATA keys. Specify direct assessment of the painful site and use relevant but insufficient remote/general findings.
issues: Two only-options cue SATA keys. Specify direct assessment of the painful site and use relevant but insufficient remote/general findings.

options: The total score on the most recent pressure-risk tool
Local warmth or coolness compared with surrounding skin
Changes in firmness or skin colour from baseline
The colour documented at admission without re-examining the area
why: The score informs prevention but does not directly examine the painful sacral tissue.
Temperature differences may reveal early tissue change.
Texture and baseline comparison support assessment across skin tones.
Baseline is useful for comparison, but current local examination is necessary.
proposedChanges.stem: An immobile client with darkly pigmented skin reports sacral tenderness without obvious redness. Which current local findings best help assess possible pressure-related tissue change? Select all that apply.

items.assessment: Smaller supported changes with pain management balance relief with tolerance. Dressing-only and forced large turns fail to address the problem. Learning objective overlaps basic121 in a non-end-of-life setting; avoid adjacent presentation.

Approved assisted inspection preserves alignment while addressing concealed device pressure. Independent removal, altered padding and visible-only checks are relevant collar-care errors; local training remains necessary.
A ring-cushion pressure mark supports individualized seating review. Stacking, taut covering and extending exposure are plausible but ineffective adjustments.
Only qualifiers reveal SATA keys. Keep comparable observations but target outcome rather than process.
issues: Only qualifiers reveal SATA keys. Keep comparable observations but target outcome rather than process.

options: The number of pillows recorded on the positioning chart
Skin condition at vulnerable sites
Comfort and tolerance between turns
The percentage of scheduled turns documented as completed
why: The count does not establish actual offloading or tissue response.
Tissue response shows whether protection is effective.
The plan must be feasible and acceptable for the client.
Adherence is useful process information but does not itself demonstrate comfort or tissue protection.
proposedChanges.stem: Which observations most directly show whether an individualized turning plan is protecting the client while remaining tolerable? Select all that apply.

items.assessment: An observed folded-pad ridge is an immediately correctable pressure source. Removal and skin reassessment is appropriately direct rather than delaying for analgesia or linen routine.
Tighten-sleeve/remove-dressing/stop-arm-use alternatives are extreme. Use practical but incomplete workaround choices.
issues: Tighten-sleeve/remove-dressing/stop-arm-use alternatives are extreme. Use practical but incomplete workaround choices.

options: Wear a snug sleeve over the dressing to hold the edges flat
Trim the dressing edges until they no longer catch
Avoid the usual upper-body activities until the next dressing change
Review dressing securement and clothing contact
why: Extra contact pressure and friction may worsen trauma; assess dressing and clothing fit.
Unplanned trimming may compromise coverage or product function; review securement and clothing contact first.
A correctable snagging problem may be solved without unnecessary functional restriction.
Reducing traction protects the wound and improves comfort.

items.assessment: Distributed leg support without popliteal compression fits the supplied venous-elevation plan and intact arterial circulation. Narrow edge, new numbness and focal knee pressure are meaningful warning alternatives.
Colour/brand distraction is superficial and staff should correct constriction. Replace with an apparently reasonable sizing shortcut.
issues: Colour/brand distraction is superficial and staff should correct constriction. Replace with an apparently reasonable sizing shortcut.

options: Replace it with the next larger size without remeasuring the limb
Remove the constricting roll and reassess fit
Add tape to hold the roll
Leave it because tighter pressure is more effective
why: Rolling may reflect application or sizing problems; reassess fit rather than guessing a size.
A rolled edge creates focal pressure rather than prescribed graduated compression.
Tape preserves the constricting configuration.
Excess local pressure is not the therapeutic goal.

items.assessment: Report question contains inference plus actions/only qualifiers. Use parallel interpretations.
issues: Report question contains inference plus actions/only qualifiers. Use parallel interpretations.

options: Maceration and inadequate exudate management
Expected moisture from a healthy granulating wound
Likely infection because the dressing remains wet
Dry skin requiring a thicker layer of moisturizer
why: Excess retained moisture can damage surrounding skin.
Repeated saturation and white soggy surrounding skin suggest excess moisture injury rather than balanced wound moisture.
Wetness alone does not establish infection; the described surrounding-skin change points to maceration.
The tissue is overhydrated, so additional moisturizer does not address the described mechanism.

items.assessment: The adhesive-outline distribution with an improving wound makes product irritation a relevant possibility. Key appropriately assesses rather than diagnoses definitively; increasing exposure or abandoning protection is inappropriate.

Reviewing fixation/removal methods addresses recurrent adhesive trauma; stronger adhesion, friction and rotating the same trauma are recognizable misconceptions. Product choice remains individualized.
Mirror or agreed assistance resolves inaccessible soles when sensation is reduced. Temperature, pain and footwear discomfort cannot substitute for visual inspection.
The seam-matching mark identifies an immediate mechanical source; remove and reassess. More bulk, symptom waiting and cream alone do not fix pressure.
Only moisture response and heavy blankets make SATA keys trivial. Narrow the objective and use plausible but insufficient responses.
issues: Only moisture response and heavy blankets make SATA keys trivial. Narrow the objective and use plausible but insufficient responses.

options: Reassess temperature and hydration needs
Place a waterproof pad beneath the client and keep the damp clothing in place
Increase bedding insulation to prevent chilling while the client remains damp
Replace damp clothing and linens
why: Sweating may accompany fluid losses and evolving illness.
A pad does not remove existing moisture against the skin or restore comfort.
Assess comfort and illness rather than adding heavy insulation over damp clothing.
Removing moisture supports comfort and skin protection.

items.assessment: The helpful preference is already named, and distractors are coercive routines. Test integrating the position with prevention through plausible plans.
issues: The helpful preference is already named, and distractors are coercive routines. Test integrating the position with prevention through plausible plans.

options: Use the preferred position for the whole shift to maximize pain relief
Reserve the preferred position until after the standard turn sequence is complete
Incorporate it with appropriate support and skin assessment
Use the preferred position whenever requested without checking the skin
why: A helpful position still needs review of pressure exposure and individual tolerance.
An inflexible sequence may unnecessarily postpone a safe relieving position.
Preference can be honoured while maintaining pressure management.
Preference can be respected while still monitoring pressure-related tissue response.

items.assessment: Swelling changes device fit; inspect skin/circulation and review fitting. Padding or tightening a tight boot increases pressure. The key appropriately integrates assessment without prescribing an unsupported device alteration.
Extra clothing is filler and only total-time option is cued. Use duration-related planning competitors.
issues: Extra clothing is filler and only total-time option is cued. Use duration-related planning competitors.

options: Shorter sitting periods with assessed pressure relief
Continue three hours because skin is still intact
Keep the three-hour session but use an additional cushion without reviewing fit
Maintain the same total sitting time and reassess at the weekly review
why: The observed duration-related response guides progression.
Pain can signal tissue stress before visible breakdown.
Adding equipment does not establish safe pressure distribution or tolerated duration.
New duration-related discomfort should guide the next session, not wait for routine review.

issues: Fragrance-only and any-home-product claims are obvious. Use competing sources of relevant but insufficient evidence.

Whether the product was tolerated on another uncovered area
Whether the client has used the same product for several years
Product compatibility and its effect on the seal

items.assessment: Observed taught turn and skin check demonstrate both performance and monitoring. Verbal equipment knowledge alone is a plausible incomplete evaluation. Waiting for redness or persisting through new pain shows unsafe understanding.

overlapNotes: basic132 repeats the tolerated-repositioning objective of121 in a different goals-of-care context. Keep separate in practice sets or choose one in curated modes.
sourceCheckLimit: No new procedure-specific source sweep for this routine skin-care batch. Pressure offloading/dark-skin assessment concepts were checked against primary NICE guidance in the legacy review; no claim of complete clinical validation is made.
